opening_message:
Ticket 1: Robert Weber (employee ID E047) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E047.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Robert Weber (E047) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted for his role. Full-time employees max out at write for systems they don't own, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E047 is a contractor with basic security training (note: HR lists full_time; security record shows contractor). As a contractor, max is read without advanced training, and admin is never permitted for contractors. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Robert Weber (E047) is a full-time Payroll Specialist per the HR database (verified). Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Payroll Specialist, so admin is not permitted under the policy (admin only if the employee's role owns the system; full-time employees max out at write for systems they don't own). The requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum (write), so the maximum is granted.

- recommendation for Source Code: write

Security agent note:
- role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up; same as HR)
- employment type: contractor (looked up in own database)
- security training: basic (looked up)
- recommendation: read
- Comment: Security DB shows contractor with basic training. As contractor, max is read without advanced training; admin never permitted for contractors. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read.

The conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor.

How do we resolve? The notes say HR looked up employment type in own database. Security also looked up employment type in own database. Conflicting facts. Hmm.

We need to make a decision. The policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Either way, admin is not permitted for Source Code because:
- If full_time: max is write (role Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code; Engineer owns it).
- If contractor: max is read (basic training) or write (advanced), never admin.

So regardless of employment type, admin is above maximum. The requested level is admin, which exceeds max. So grant the maximum.

Now, what is the maximum? It depends on employment type and training:
- If full_time: write
- If contractor with basic training: read

HR recommends write; Security recommends read.

Hmm, an important consideration: the HR agent is the authoritative source for employment type. But the security agent's database also lists it. This is a designed conflict.

When facts conflict, we need to decide which is more reliable. But there's no way to know ground truth.

So admin request → grant max. Full-time max is write; contractor max is read. The discrepancy matters for whether max is write or read.

Which to choose? Let me think about the source. HR's database is the authoritative employment database. Security databases may have stale/incorrect employment type. The HR note explicitly says "looked up in own database" and the security note says "security DB shows contractor". 

Hmm. In previous similar tasks I've seen, when HR and Security conflict on employment type, the HR record is generally the correct one for employment type because HR manages employment. I'll go with full_time → max write.
